Opposite Party :- The State Of U.P. Thru.Prin.Secy. Deptt. Of Home And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Firoz Ahmad Khan
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Om Prakash Tripathi Tiwari,Om Prakash Tripathi,Prabha
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.

Heard Shri Firoz Ahmad Khan, learned counsel for the accused/applicant and Shri Om Prakash
Tripathi, learned counsel appearing for opposite party no.2 as well as learned A.G.A. for the State
and perused the record.

2. This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Mohammad Arshad for grant of
bail, in Case Crime No. 212/2022, under Sections 363, 376-D, 376Da, 305, 342, 506 Ipc and
Section 3/4, 5/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Police Station
Malipur, District Ambedkar Nagar, during trial.

The First Information Report of this case was lodged by the father of the victim on 16.9.2022 against some unknown persons, stating therein that on 16.9.2022 his daughter had gone to the school but did not return.
She is a student of Class-VIII of Nawab Husain Inter Mohammad Arshad vs The State Of U.P. Thru.Prin.Secy. ...

1 College, Hajpura.
The age of the victim/ prosecutrix is shown as 13 years.

On 18.9.2022 an application was again moved by the informant stating therein that the prosecutrix had returned home in the morning of 18.9.2022 and on being inquired stated that she was abducted by two persons who were driving a Maruti Car and one Mohd. Arshad (applicant) who is a resident of Katghar Moosa was standing nearby and those two unknown persons had committed rape on her.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant vehemently submits that in the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she had only stated that the applicant was standing nearby when she was abducted by the two unknown persons in the vehicle bearing Registration No. U.P. 32 HS 135 and she was taken to a hotel where she was raped, however, she declined to identify the two persons who have committed rape on her and also did not disclose the name of the hotel.

5. While drawing attention of this Court towards the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., it is vehemently submitted that in this statement of the prosecutrix, the victim/
prosecutrix had not mentioned the presence of the applicant on the spot at all and thus the involvement of the applicant in this case is only on account of his association with one Meera Upadhyaya with whom the informant's family is having property dispute.

6. While drawing the attention of this Court towards the statement of Meera Upadhyay (aunt of the victim/ deceased), it is submitted that the applicant used to visit the house of Meera Upadhyay on account of his association with the husband of Meera Upadhyay and the informant's party was inimical towards her (Meera Upadhyay) on account of the frequent visit of the applicant to her house.

7. It is vehemently submitted that even if the case of the prosecution is believed as it is, the same may not attract any imputation against the applicant and the charge sheet against the applicant has been filed without there being any sufficient material/ evidence.
8. It is further submitted that the applicant is in jail in this case since 7.10.2022.
Charge sheet in this case has already been submitted and the applicant is not having any criminal history.
There is no apprehension that the accused-applicant after release on bail, may flee from the process of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
9. Learned A.G.A., however, opposes the prayer for bail but could not dispute the other factual submissions made by the learned counsel for the accused-applicant.

10. Shri Om Prakash Tripathi, learned counsel for opposite party no.2 vehemently opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that the prosecutrix/ victim aged about 13 years old was not only raped but also committed suicide on 5.10.2022 and the presence of the applicant has been shown in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. near the place from where she had been abducted and having regard to the fact that Meera Upadhyay is highly inimical towards the family of the informant and she is having close association with the instant applicant, the offence in all probability has been committed by the applicant.

Attention of this court has also been drawn towards an FIR lodged by one Roshani Upadhyay on 20.4.2023 at P.S. Malipur, District Ambedkar Mohammad Arshad vs The State Of U.P. Thru.Prin.Secy. ... on 17 August, 2023

Nagar against Meera pertaining to setting ablaze the house of the informant of that case and it is submitted that Meera Upadhyay after being granted bail had set ablaze the residential house of the informant and the applicant being her close associate should not be granted the facility of bail.

11. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it would emerge that the father of the prosecutrix is informant of the case and FIR of this case was lodged by him on 16.9.2022 stating therein that his daughter (victim/ deceased) had gone to the school at 7.00 A.M.
but did not return there after.

On 18.9.2022 the informant had moved another written application wherein it is mentioned that on 18.9.2022 at about 6.30 A.M. the prosecutrix had returned home herself and had informed that she was abducted by the two unknown persons in a Maruti Car and was taken to a hotel where she was raped and the applicant was standing nearby.

In the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. the prosecutrix/ victim maintained the story as narrated by his father in the application given on 18.9.2022 that she was abducted by two unknown persons and the applicant was standing nearby.

However, in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
before the Magistrate she did not impute any allegation at all against the instant applicant and even did not mention his presence on spot from where she was abducted.

During the course of investigation the Investigating Officer has recorded the statements of sister of the prosecutrix (her name is being not mentioned for the sake of privacy) and also of her brother wherein they both have stated that as per the information collected by them, the instant applicant was standing at the place from where the victim was abducted and they are having apprehension/ suspicion that Meera Upadhyay and applicant may have a hand in the commission of the crime.

During the course of investigation the vehicle, Registration number of which was mentioned by the victim was also traced and the statement of the owner of that vehicle was also recorded and it was found that this vehicle was not involved in the incident and thus, he was given clean chit by the Investigating Officer.

It is also reflected from the record and also from the First Information report, a copy of which has been placed for perusal by learned counsel for opposite party no.2 that the informant's party of this case is having some property dispute with their aunt namely Meera Upadhyay.

Thus, the whole evidence which has been collected by the Investigating Officer and the statement of the prosecution witnesses would reflect only one thing that when the victim was allegedly abducted by the two unknown persons, the applicant was shown to be standing nearby and beyond that there was no whisper about any illegal act of the applicant.

It is also pertinent to mention here that during the course of investigation the prosecutrix had also committed suicide and the applicant along with other accused persons is also charge-sheeted under Section 306 IPC.

One more thing which would be relevant is that during the course of investigation the Investigating Officer has also recorded the statement of one Ms. Swati who had stated that the prosecutrix while going and coming from the school used to go to the shop of one Ankesh and used to talk with him and also click photographs and during this period she ( Swati) used to stand outside the shop.
It is also stated by her that the deceased was also talking a lot with Ankesh on mobile phone.

12. Thus, keeping in view all the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence which has been placed against the applicant, in the considered opinion of this case his role has been shown of only standing near the place from where the prosecutrix/victim had been allegedly abducted and beyond that there is no whisper either in the counter affidavit filed by the state or anywhere else about any over act of the applicant.

Thus, in the considered opinion of this court, facility of bail may Mohammad Arshad vs The State Of U.P. Thru.Prin.Secy. ... on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112741383/
3 be extended to the applicant more so when he is not having any criminal antecedent and is in jail in this case since 07.10.2022.

sentences.text: Apprehension of the complainant may be taken care of by placing adequate conditions on the applicant.

13. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits and demerits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

14. Let the applicant- Mohammad Arshad involved in the aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not attempt to contact the informant or any of his family member including the prosecution witnesses directly or indirectly or through any social media platform.
(ii) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(iii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iv) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
15.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
16. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
17. Observations made herein-above are only for the purpose of disposal of bail application and the same shall not have any bearing on the trial of the case.
